task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's output for REQ-037 (27 tests across 2 files + test/specs/REQ-037.md). Read the spec and both test files independently -- do not trust TEST-DESIGNER's own handoff summary. Verify against REQ-037's actual 6 acceptance_criteria in docs/requirements.yaml and the validated design. Specifically re-check: (1) AC4's concurrency test genuinely runs 2 concurrent Task.async processes with a real synchronization barrier, not a sequential simulation dressed up to look concurrent -- read the test code and confirm both approve_review/4 calls are actually in-flight simultaneously before either completes; (2) the 7-edges + 2-non-edges test in AC6 actually asserts the identical :invalid_transition atom for both non-edge attempts, not just 'an error'; (3) the insert_review/2 tenant_id-from-prefix test genuinely constructs a case where plan.target_tenant_id disagrees with the prefix-derived tenant, and asserts the STORED row (re-read from Postgres) has the prefix-derived value, not the plan's; (4) fixtures use per-test unique tenant schemas with no cross-test pollution risk against real Postgres.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-037 acceptance criterion has at least one runnable test that would actually fail if the behavior were violated
AC4's concurrency mechanism is genuinely concurrent (both Task.async processes verifiably in-flight together via the barrier), not sequential
AC6's non-edge tests assert the identical :invalid_transition atom explicitly for both illegal transitions tested
insert_review/2's prefix-vs-plan tenant_id test re-reads the stored row from Postgres and asserts the prefix-derived value won
No 'TODO: implement test' or skipped test left anywhere
Test fixtures use per-test unique tenant/data -- verify directly
Independently re-run MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test on the 2 new files and confirm the reported 27/27 pass count is real

result.summary: Independently read test/specs/REQ-037.md and both test files (not the TEST-DESIGNER handoff summary). All 6 REQ-037 acceptance criteria (verified against the verbatim acceptance_criteria list in docs/requirements.yaml, not just the spec's paraphrase) each have >=1 runnable test that would fail if the behavior were violated. Specific re-checks: (1) AC4's concurrency test (promotion_review_store_test.exs:428-480) genuinely spawns 2 Task.async processes that each send {:ready, self()} then block on `receive do :go -> :ok after 5000 -> flunk(...) end` before calling approve_review/4; the parent asserts both {:ready, pid} messages, confirms pid1 != pid2, then sends :go to both -- byte-for-byte the same barrier idiom as test/letflow/event_store_test.exs's 'concurrent appends (AC2)' test (lines 353-401), not a superficial/sequential imitation. Sandbox mode is :auto (via provisioned_tenant/0), so each Task gets its own independent Postgres connection, making the race real. (2) AC6's two required non-edge tests (rejected->approved, pending_review->applied) both assert the literal identical atom: `assert result_a == {:error, :invalid_transition}`, `assert result_b == {:error, :invalid_transition}`, plus `assert Enum.uniq([result_a, result_b]) == [{:error, :invalid_transition}]` (lines 627-632) -- not two different atoms, not just 'an error'. (3) insert_review/2's prefix-vs-plan tenant_id test (lines 272-304) builds plan.target_tenant_id as a fresh, unrelated Ecto.UUID.generate() that is asserted (refute) to differ from the real provisioned tenant_id, then after insert re-reads the row via `Repo.get!(PromotionReview, review.id, prefix: schema_name)` (a fresh Postgres read, not the in-memory {:ok, review} reply) and asserts persisted.tenant_id == real_tenant_id / refute == disagreeing_target_tenant_id, plus confirms the plan's disagreeing value is still stored verbatim in serialised_plan (proving the disagreement was genuine). (4) Fixtures: every test provisions its own tenant via insert_tenant!/provisioned_tenant (slug suffixed with System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])), real CREATE SCHEMA + TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1, Sandbox :auto mode with manual on_exit/1 DROP SCHEMA CASCADE + row cleanup -- no shared/hardcoded tenant/process-key/review ids anywhere; every identifier is Ecto.UUID.generate() or System.unique_integer/1. Tests are self-sufficient (each provisions/tears down its own state, async: false module-wide avoids ordering assumptions but no test reads another test's data). No TODO/skip found (grep clean), no hardcoded secrets/connection strings (grep clean -- only docker-compose.yml has the dev Postgres password, not these test files). Independently re-ran `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs` against real Postgres (docker compose postgres service): actual output '27 tests, 0 failures', 'Finished in 4.0 seconds (0.00s async, 4.0s sync)' -- confirms TEST-DESIGNER's reported 27/27 is real, not a self-report taken on trust.
